The last few days have been focused on improving the robustness of the ApplyOS (live at applyos.io) platform. Specifically, I've been working through a large batch of ESLint errors.

It might seem like a small task, but addressing these issues has led to cleaner, more predictable code, especially in areas handling external data and AI interactions. We're aiming for a more resilient system, so these foundational steps are crucial.

One area that saw a lot of refinement was how we handle type assertions and data parsing. It's a constant balancing act: making the code flexible enough to handle variations in external data while maintaining type safety. Explicitly casting and checking types, even when it feels a bit verbose, prevents subtle bugs down the line.

What's your approach to managing type safety in rapidly evolving codebases?
